note: The queue behind `node scripts/actions.mjs`. Skills write items here; the board renders them and writes the result back into the repo when every step of a card is checked. Keep `steps` to things SHIVAM does with his own hands — anything Claude does is not a step, it is a sentence in `background`.

items.title: SingleStore: new-grad Software Engineer, India, no years bar, C++ + systems fundamentals
items.sub: Distributed SQL database. University-grad seat (query optimiser, SIMD/LLVM codegen, fault tolerance). Dossier + tech-read done; resume not tailored yet. Likely office-based (Bangalore/Hyderabad/Pune), ~10-16L reported.
steps: Decide: are you OK working from a SingleStore office in India (Bangalore/Hyderabad/Pune)? If not, tick everything and pass
Tell Claude roughly how much C/C++ you've actually written (CP only, or projects too)
Press Work it so Claude tailors the resume for this req
items.background: The HN post was for the AI Platform req (4+ years, mentoring), which is C. This new-grad req has no years bar and asks for C/C++, OS/concurrency, algorithms; your CSE degree (May 2026), LeetCode top 5% and CodeSM's sandboxed C/C++ runner carry it. Gap: no professional C++ or engine work. Channel is the Greenhouse form (resume, LinkedIn, website, optional cover letter). The HN poster is on another team, so the warmer path is an IIIT Nagpur alum at SingleStore via /network-scout, not checked yet. Two internals questions are in tech-read.md.

items.title: Trackerbot: Node.js + Postgres, fully remote, €35-45k, email goes straight to the CTO
items.sub: Profitable 3-person team in Sofia. Gmail draft and tailored CV (ATS 88) are ready; attach the PDF and send.
steps: Read the draft to dobrev.d10@gmail.com and change anything that doesn't sound like you
Attach applications/trackerbot/resume.pdf
Send it
items.background: Their app is Express on Heroku with session affinity across 5+ web dynos, plus two Chrome extensions that upload trackings from the seller's browser in non-API mode. Worst public review: 50 orders not uploaded for five days. The email leads with that kind of silent stall and your CodeSM/Hireflow queue work, and names the gaps (no Chrome extension, no eBay/Amazon API). Two call questions are in outreach.md.

items.title: Interview Resources: back-end AI engineer, remote, and their open problems are three things you've built
items.sub: Solo founder, profitable, remote at $30k-$90k adjusted for location. The role is the research pipeline: move a multi-minute run off the request path, a credits ledger, LLM output that has to be correct. Storix, klimb.io and Hireflow. The catch: they ask for 4+ years. The message says so plainly.
steps: Pick your expected salary and check your poiro.com notice period
Rewrite the draft message in your own words (he asks for human-written)
Paste it into the form and submit it yourself
items.background: Their public repo shows the whole research run executing inline in the POST route (maxDuration 300, SSE), a reserve/settle credit ledger with row locks and unique-ref idempotency, and a reaper route that claims to be run by Vercel Cron while vercel.json has no crons key. That last one is the question in the message: it can't be wrong, and only someone who read the code would ask it. Follow-up X DM for 2026-10-06 is drafted in outreach.md. Harsh (the repo's previous owner) applied here 2026-09-04; this is Shivam's own application.

items.title: CyberAtlas: remote-worldwide backend + data pipelines on 2.5B domains, no years bar
items.sub: Python/FastAPI, Redis, MongoDB/Postgres, Docker, all true for you. The email and a tailored CV (ATS 88) are ready; it needs one thing only you can do: their anti-bot Finder query.
steps: Run one query on Finder yourself and copy the query + first page of results
Paste both into the email in outreach.md, read it, cut anything you wouldn't say
Send from shivam.verma.dev00@gmail.com to atlas@cyberatlas.ai with resume.pdf attached
items.background: Their API headers show the architecture: exact-root queries page as a key-value range scan (kv: cursor), a *vpn*.io substring query reports a 54.6M-row scan of the whole .io partition and still answers in ~1.5s, and every query is metered against a daily domain budget. The email asks the one question that falls out of that. Gaps named plainly: no Go, no OpenSearch, nothing near billions of rows.

items.title: OpenAlex: submit the Software Engineer form
items.sub: Remote, $150-200k, no years bar. Resume + 3 answers + pack.json ready. One-shot form, so read before you click.
steps: Create an OpenAlex account with shivam.verma.dev00@gmail.com and set your name in settings
Read the 3 answers aloud in answers.md and fix anything that isn't you
Fill the form (extension or paste), set degree to Bachelor's, paste resume.md
Review every field and click Submit application
items.background: Their API front door is a Cloudflare Worker that prices each request in credits, counts it in a Durable Object and settles prepaid balances into Postgres, the same object as your klimb.io credit ledger. The first-week answer asks two questions verified in their source: the claim-then-UPDATE writeback inside waitUntil, and refunds after UTC midnight landing on the new day's counter. Gaps named plainly: Spark/Databricks, Elasticsearch, scale, ~8 months. Tracker already logged as sent (folder-complete rule); say 'hold' if you apply later.

items.title: Send the SerpApi application email
items.sub: Junior Fullstack, worldwide, published address. Drafted only: the C lane isn't authorised to send for you yet.
steps: Read the draft in outreach.md and cut anything you wouldn't say
Send it to careers@serpapi.com with applications/serpapi/resume.pdf attached
items.background: Stack is Ruby/Rails/MongoDB/JS on Linux+AWS; you have no Ruby, and the email says so. The seam is Hireflow: 4-source scraping + Playwright with stages on separate BullMQ queues so a bot-detection block doesn't stall the rest (their JD lists scraping and browser tech as a plus). Resume ~80 self-scored, one pass, Ruby/Rails honestly absent. Gmail prior-contact check could not run (Gmail connector not authenticated); no folder on disk. C lane: one touch, follow-up none.

items.title: Send the VLM Run email
items.sub: Founding Infra, email-only apply. Honest gap: no GPU work. Drafted, not sent.
steps: Read the draft and decide if a founding infra seat with no GPU experience is worth one email
Send it to hiring@vlm.run with applications/vlm-run/resume.pdf attached
items.background: Only listing is the HN post (2026-09-02); no careers page or ATS board exists. Location and years unstated. They ask for GitHub + recent projects with docker, k8s, GPUs. You have Docker (CodeSM) and Kubernetes (Yuvro), no GPUs; the email says so and asks about model placement across cards instead of claiming anything. Resume is the base resume, not scored (JD too thin to score against). c-queue held it only because the lead had no link; the channel is published.

items.title: Colonist: answer 5 fields or pass
items.sub: Ashby form needs a Colonist player profile, a game quiz, your AI numbers, salary, and a no-AI motivation line.
steps: Decide: do you actually play board games? If not, tick this and pass
items.background: Held by the C lane: required fields need a colonist.io account and profile URL, knowledge of the game (max players quiz), your own AI speed-up number and example, a salary in USD/month (TODO in facts.yaml), and a 200-char motivation marked 'Please don't use AI.' The 150-word 'something you built' answer is drafted in answers-raw-material.md. The seat is UI/React-heavy and asks for 'deep' full-stack experience, so it's a weak fit for your backend profile. If you do want it: open the form, use the raw material, and ask me for a full-stack resume first (none is tailored for Colonist yet).
